rule_definition.name: READY Required Before Certification Board Review

rule_text: No item shall enter a Certification Board review unless its Framework v2 readiness classification is READY (all gates PASS) or MINOR_FIX (SOFT_FAIL with acknowledged warnings). Items classified as BLOCKED or REMEDIATE are excluded from Certification Board queues. This rule prevents the v1 pattern where 89.5% of items entering certification boards carried hidden structural defects.

enforcement.mechanism: Pre-Certification Board gate check. The Readiness Scorer (S322 Script 7) produces readiness_classification per item in the Certification Scan Artifact. The Certification Board consumer (per S202.1 Board Consumption Matrix §D, sections 4+6) queries the artifact before any certification action.
enforcement.technical_implementation: Certification Board agent script reads certification_scan_artifact.json → filters items where readiness_classification == 'READY' OR (readiness_classification == 'MINOR_FIX' AND certification_warnings_accepted == true). All other items are removed from the certification queue.
enforcement.violation_consequence: If a Certification Board certifies a REMEDIATE or BLOCKED item, the certification is void. The item is re-classified REMEDIATE at the next scan. A governance exception must be filed and approved by a Governance Board member.

evidence_basis.v1_problem: S200 Agent C found 89.5% readiness failure rate — 34/38 seeds had 2+ defects when entering certification boards. S809 confirmed 38/38 seeds were HOLD at Gate 2. Boards wasted 56 agent-spawns on items that could not be certified without prior remediation.
evidence_basis.v2_solution: Readiness Engine pre-classifies every item before board entry. Only READY items (0 defects) and MINOR_FIX items (acknowledged warnings only) reach the Certification Board. REMEDIATE items are routed to remediation worklists, not certification boards.
evidence_basis.s204_validation: S204 Board E confirmed 89.5% → 0.0% hard defect leakage. 70/2,221 Certified items flagged REMEDIATE (not READY). 1,601 items READY. The rule correctly gates certification board access.

impact_on_workflows.certification_board: Board queue is pre-filtered. Board only sees READY + acknowledged MINOR_FIX items. Review time per session: from ~6 hours (scanning + reviewing all items) to ~2 hours (reviewing only ready items).
impact_on_workflows.remediation_worklist: REMEDIATE items are auto-routed to a remediation queue with specific defect flags and suggested fixes. No board resource wasted on discovering known defects.
impact_on_workflows.governance_board: BLOCKED items (Gate -1 identity failures) are flagged immediately. No downstream processing occurs. Governance Board receives identity-block reports at scan time, not after wasted review cycles.

interaction_with_other_rules.R7 (Identity Validation): R6 depends on R7 — identity-validated scan results are a prerequisite for readiness classification. Items failing R7 are BLOCKED, never reaching the R6 gate.
interaction_with_other_rules.R8 (Scan Once): R6 consumes readiness_classification from the scan artifact (R8 product). No independent readiness scan is executed at the Certification Board.
interaction_with_other_rules.Governance Guard R2: R2 (EW[CC] empty) is a content-level rule. R6 is a pipeline-level rule. R2 is enforced by Gate 1 PG-001; R6 is enforced by the Certification Board consumer. Both must pass for certification.

example_application.scenario: S206 certification wave: 100 items enter the pipeline.
example_application.pre_r6_gates: Gate -1: 1 BLOCKED (P1-E-R33). Gate 1: 54 REMEDIATE (DL-008), 3 REMEDIATE (DL-026). Gate 2: 42 MINOR_FIX (EV3 + DL-031). 0 items REMEDIATE at Gate 3 or Gate 4.
example_application.certification_board_queue: 42 MINOR_FIX + 0 READY = 42 items. 58 items excluded (1 BLOCKED, 57 REMEDIATE).
example_application.without_r6: 100 items enter the board. Board spends ~4 hours discovering the 57 HARD_FAIL items that could not be certified.
example_application.with_r6: 42 items enter the board. Board spends ~1.5 hours certifying MINOR_FIX items with acknowledged warnings.
